title: GitLab week 6 review - deploying to environments
description: Eight questions on environments, SSH deploys, gates, review apps and Kubernetes.

questions.prompt: What do you gain by adding environment: to a deploy job?

options.text: Deployment tracking, a URL button, history, rollback and environment-scoped variables

questions.explanation: A deploy without environment: is invisible to the platform.

questions.prompt: A variable must have different values in staging and production under one name. Which mechanism?
questions.explanation: Scope the same name to each environment (wildcards like review/* work).

questions.prompt: What does SSH_KNOWN_HOSTS protect against in a deploy job?

options.text: A man-in-the-middle presenting a fake host - StrictHostKeyChecking=no would accept it

questions.explanation: Verify the host key; never disable checking in a pipeline.

questions.prompt: Which two keys turn a deploy job into a blocking manual gate?
questions.explanation: Without allow_failure: false the pipeline continues past a manual job.

questions.prompt: What stops a feature-branch pipeline from deploying to production even if its YAML has such a job?

options.text: Protected environments (deploy only from protected refs, by allowed users) plus protected branches

questions.explanation: Protection is a platform rule, not a YAML convention.

questions.prompt: Why is GIT_STRATEGY: none set on the stop-review job?

options.text: The branch may be deleted by the time it runs; it must not need a checkout

questions.explanation: Stop jobs run on merge/close, possibly after the branch is gone.

questions.prompt: What does the GitLab agent for Kubernetes remove from the pipeline compared with a kubeconfig variable?

options.text: A long-lived cluster credential in a variable and an inbound firewall hole

questions.explanation: The agent connects outbound and GitLab injects a scoped KUBECONFIG for allowed projects.

questions.prompt: Why helm --wait / kubectl rollout status rather than just apply?

options.text: So the job's exit code means 'the new pods are ready', not 'the manifest was accepted'

questions.explanation: A deploy is not done until the service answers.
